# carry

Produce the present account and commitment interface for the next complete template invocation. The material may support a revision, an unresolved problem, or retaining something. Preserve the grounds needed for whatever uptake you propose.

## Original problem (task)
[d31d61f36df18c74] (h005.task.v1)
I share a flat with two friends. We keep arguing about ordinary household chores. Sometimes we agree on who will do something, but later we disagree about what the agreement meant. Our work schedules change, and one friend has started avoiding the conversations. What should I do?

BODY
Where the inquiry stands: the objection and the rival converge more than they compete, and the work here is assembly plus a few prunings. One provenance note: the objection's target references use an artifact label that does not match the exposed account; I read them as the account's a-records by content, which is the only coherent reading.

Central revision. I accept the objection's b4 and the rival's m2 together, and they jointly revise the account's a4: the written-agreement trial should be run as a diagnostic instrument with a pre-registered verdict question, not proposed as the fix. Concretely: two weeks of one-line shared records (who, what counts as done, by when), with a question written down on day one — "after two weeks, are we still arguing, and about what?" — and three pre-named branches. (i) Disputes vanish: recall was the driver, and the account's fuller system, weekly reset included, is worth building. (ii) Disputes mutate into what-counts fights, exceptions, tone: standards or interest is the driver, and ownership domains, rotating full weeks, or a cleaner if budget allows become the indicated moves. (iii) The trial is refused, gamed, or produces no recordable agreements: attempt one structured one-time ownership conversation (turn-picking for the unequal split), then unilateral scope declaration, then the viability question the account closed with. This folding absorbs several objections at once: b4's fix, since the success criterion is the verdict question itself; b5's narrowing, since drafting-table fights become branch-(ii) evidence rather than trial failure; and the rival's q1 caveat, since non-production of agreements is itself branch-(iii) data, so the avoider's silence cannot quietly void the test.

What this does to the hard objections. The motivated-vagueness worry (b1) is real, and the objection is honest that it is as speculative as the memory reading it challenges. The fix-framing had to assume innocence; the diagnostic framing assumes nothing. Someone who games the record — litigating criteria, neglecting to record, retro-narrowing — produces exactly the pattern that sorts the household into branch (ii) or (iii). Gaming becomes data instead of defeat. This does not fully resolve b6: a cheerful attender who games everything still gets no direct remedy from anything on the table. The branches route around such a person, and if routing fails, the question lands where the account's a8 said it would. I would rather name that limit than paper over it.

The channel needs the objection's b2 correction, and I accept it: participation in conversation is not contribution to household labor, and counting edits as "full participation" certified the wrong thing. The channel survives as a low-cost input route — the meta-conversation still needs the avoiding friend reachable — but contribution gets judged by observable outcomes. The decoupling branches make that easy: an owned domain's state is visible without the owner attending anything, which adopts the rival's design principle (o2) — make the system work even if they never participate — rather than merely nodding at it.

On b3 and the institutional reframing (c1–c3): "coordinate less" was a genuine omission, and decoupling now sits in the branch table. But I decline to accept the institutional diagnosis as a premise. Ordering answers the proportionality worry: the minimal record costs almost nothing, so the household pays bureaucratization costs only if the cheap test says coordination infrastructure would fix the actual driver, and pays decoupling's own relocation cost (q2: the initial split of unequal domains is itself a negotiation among people currently failing to negotiate) only when evidence points there. Recall failure and institution failure are both live hypotheses; the trial is how a household that cannot settle arguments from memory finds out which one it is living in.

One caution I add, aimed at the rival's m1: unilateral scope declaration converts a coordination failure into a contest of tolerances and spends friendship capital by design — the visible lapse is leverage. It is rational only late, after a structured attempt has failed, and only if the asker can genuinely outlast the others' indifference to undone chores. It also sits in tension with a6's separation of friendship from chore-negotiation, and anyone using it should know they are suspending that protection.

What survives untouched: a6 (calm scheduled meta-conversation, pattern not incident, friendship kept separate) — the objection explicitly spares it and the rival retains it via u1; the viability flag (a8); and a7's warning that clarity can expose unfairness, now absorbed into branch (ii), where an exposed imbalance is handled by turn-picking or renegotiation of the split itself rather than left as a surprise. The bookkeeping point that the weekly reset had no commitments record is resolved by moving it into branch (i).

What I reject: a4's stated consequence — disputes being "checkable against a record" covers less ground than promised, per b5 and o1 — and the framing of writing as remedy rather than instrument; a5's "full participation" clause; and any version of either framing that treats the driver as already known.

So the sequence for the asker: one calm conversation about the pattern; propose the two-week minimal record with the verdict question written alongside; hand the avoiding friend the asynchronous channel as an input route; read the result against the branch table; escalate only as indicated; keep friendship talk separate throughout; hold the viability question in reserve, named in advance as the terminal branch rather than discovered as a surprise. What remains open: which driver obtains (by design — the test exists to answer it), whether the one-time ownership negotiation succeeds where informal ones failed, the standards gap, budget, remaining goodwill, and the residual gamer. None is answerable from this material, and the plan's virtue is needing none of them answered in advance.
